en: The Philippine tarsier has the largest eyes relative to its body size of any mammal.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found in Mount Apo, produces the largest flower in the Philippines.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift incubator using a bamboo basket and a hot water bottle.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park protects a highly diverse marine ecosystem containing hundreds of fish and coral species.
The waling-waling orchid, native to Mindanao, uses specialized aerial roots to absorb moisture directly from the humid air.
The Philippine eagle lays only one egg per breeding cycle, making its population growth very slow.
The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, has distinct V-shaped horns that curve backward.
Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization, a heating process that kills harmful bacteria in milk and other liquids.
Mangrove trees in Philippine coastal ecosystems grow specialized breathing roots called pneumatophores to survive in oxygen-poor mud.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito transmits the dengue virus, which causes severe flu-like symptoms in humans.
The critically endangered Philippine crocodile is a freshwater species distinct from the larger saltwater crocodile.
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek used a single-lens microscope to become the first person to observe living microorganisms.
